name: Head of Deepfury
summary: At the Stormwind Stockade, Kam Deepfury’s severed head marks the end of a Dark Iron conspirator. His death in the prison riots answers the grievance of the dwarven defenders at Dun Modr.

sections.title: A Conspirator's Justice
sections.body: Kam Deepfury was held in the Stormwind Stockade for political reasons, spared immediate execution by human diplomacy. Roggo uncovered that Deepfury had orchestrated the attack on the Thandol Span, which cost the lives of King Magni’s soldiers and Longbraid the Grim’s kin. The Ironforge mountaineers at Dun Modr could not accept his continued imprisonment. Bound to his post, Motley Garmason sent Alliance champions into the rioting prison to take Deepfury’s head and deliver dwarven vengeance.

faq.answer: Kam Deepfury was a Dark Iron dwarf who helped plan the sabotage of the Thandol Span, the land bridge between the Wetlands and the Arathi Highlands. His conspiracy cost dwarven defenders their lives, including Longbraid the Grim’s brother.

faq.q: Why was Kam Deepfury in the Stockade instead of executed?
faq.answer: Stormwind authorities held Deepfury alive for political reasons. The Ironforge mountaineers saw this restraint as an outrage and demanded his death.

faq.q: Who wants the Head of Deepfury?
faq.answer: Motley Garmason, stationed at Dun Modr in the northern Wetlands, wants the head. Bound by honor to remain at his post beside Longbraid the Grim, he sends someone to do what he cannot.

faq.q: What does bringing back the head accomplish?
faq.answer: Bringing Deepfury’s severed head to Dun Modr answers the grievance of the mourning dwarven families. It avenges Longbraid the Grim’s slain brother and shows that human political maneuvering will not bury crimes against Ironforge.

angles.text: For Ironforge dwarves, taking Deepfury’s head answers the grievance over the Dark Iron treachery at the Thandol Span.
The demand for Deepfury’s head reveals friction within the Alliance: Stormwind’s human authorities favor legal caution, while Ironforge’s mountaineers demand harsh justice.
